title: Places in America
description: Ten short stories about visits to American places: the Grand Canyon, New Orleans, Chicago, Washington, D.C., Yellowstone, a train across the north, Seattle and the coast of Maine, with a little simple geography and history, and a student studying the Mississippi River.

lessons.title: A Diary from the Grand Canyon
lessons.summary: A woman writes in her diary about her first two days at the Grand Canyon.
lessons.text:
Monday

My husband Paul and I arrived at the Grand Canyon in Arizona this afternoon. We have wanted to come here for many years, and finally we are here. We walked from our hotel to the edge of the canyon, and I saw the most amazing sight of my life.

A park ranger told us some facts. The canyon is about 277 miles long, and in some places it is about 1,800 meters deep. The edge where we were standing, the South Rim, is at a height of about 2,100 meters.

The ranger also told us that the canyon is ancient. The Colorado River has been cutting through the rock for millions of years. The elements, like water, wind and ice, have shaped the walls too. Some of the ancient rocks at the bottom are almost 2 billion years old.

In the evening, the sun went down, and the rocks turned golden, then red. It was a beautiful sight.

Tuesday

This morning we got up at 5 to watch the sun come up. The sky was bright and clear, and in the bright morning light, the walls of the canyon looked golden again.

After that, we started walking down a path into the canyon. I have to be honest: I was a little afraid. The path is narrow, and in some places there is a drop of hundreds of meters next to it. Paul put his hand on my shoulder and said, "Don't be afraid. Just look at the path, not at the drop."

The ranger had told us not to go too far, because walking back up is much harder than walking down. We walked down for 2 hours and then turned back. On the way up, my legs hurt a lot, and my bag felt heavy on my shoulder.

When we got to the top, I was tired, but very happy. If I were younger, I would walk all the way down to the river!

Questions:
Where is the Grand Canyon?
The Grand Canyon is in Arizona.
At what height is the South Rim?
The South Rim is at a height of about 2,100 meters.
How did the canyon get its shape?
The Colorado River and the elements, like water, wind and ice, shaped it over millions of years.
What color did the rocks turn in the evening?
They turned golden, then red.
Why was the writer afraid on the path?
She was afraid because the path is narrow and there is a big drop next to it.
Why did her legs hurt?
Her legs hurt because walking back up is much harder than walking down.

lessons.title: A Cooking Class in New Orleans
lessons.summary: Rosa visits New Orleans, eats a sweet breakfast, learns some history and cooks chicken gumbo in a cooking class.
lessons.text:
Rosa lived in Texas, and she loved cooking. Last spring, she took a short trip to New Orleans, a city in Louisiana near the end of the Mississippi River. Before the trip, she had already booked a cooking class.

On her first morning, Rosa went to a famous coffee shop near the river. She ordered beignets, which are small pieces of hot bread covered with sugar. They came with a large cup of coffee with hot milk. The air was filled with the smell of coffee and sugar. There was so much sugar on the beignets that her black shirt became white! The coffee with milk was strong and good.

After that, Rosa walked through the French Quarter, the oldest part of the city. A guide told her that New Orleans was originally a French city. The French had started it in 1718. Later, Spain ruled the city, and in 1803 it became part of the United States. "Many of these historical buildings were built when Spain ruled the city," the guide said. Rosa took pictures of the historical houses. The guide also said that jazz music was born in New Orleans more than 100 years ago.

At 11, Rosa went to the cooking class. The kitchen was big and bright, and it was filled with the smell of cooking. The teacher, a cook named Henry, said, "Today we are making chicken gumbo for lunch." Gumbo is a kind of soup with chicken, rice and other things. Henry told the class that every family in New Orleans has its own way to make gumbo. "My way is my mother's way," he said.

Rosa cut the chicken into small pieces. Henry showed everyone how to cook flour and oil for a long time, until it turned dark brown. "This is the most important step," he said. Soon the whole kitchen was filled with a wonderful smell.

At 1, the gumbo was ready. Everyone ate lunch together at a big table in the kitchen. It was the best lunch of Rosa's trip. "If I lived here, I would take this class every week," she told Henry. Before she left, she asked him how to make gumbo in her own kitchen at home.

Questions:
What are beignets?
Beignets are small pieces of hot bread covered with sugar.
What did Rosa drink with the beignets?
She drank a large cup of coffee with hot milk.
Who originally started New Orleans?
The French originally started New Orleans, in 1718.
What was the kitchen filled with?
The kitchen was filled with the smell of cooking.
What did the class make for lunch?
They made chicken gumbo for lunch.

lessons.title: A Weekend in Chicago
lessons.summary: Tom and his son take a boat tour in Chicago, learn about the great fire of 1871 and buy a basketball jersey.
lessons.text:
Tom and his 12-year-old son, Jack, took the train to Chicago for a weekend. Chicago is in Illinois, next to Lake Michigan.

On Saturday morning, they went on a boat tour on the Chicago River. "In 1871, there was a great fire here," the guide said. "Most buildings were made of wood, and fire can destroy wood very quickly. It took the fire only 2 days to destroy about 17,000 buildings."

Jack asked how the fire had started. "Nobody knows for sure," the guide said. "After the incident, people said that a cow had kicked over a lamp in a barn. The barn belonged to a woman named Catherine O'Leary, so many people blamed her for the incident. But in 1997, the city said officially that the fire was not her fault."

After the fire, the people of Chicago built their city again with stone and steel. New ideas enabled them to make much higher buildings. In 1885, an office building in Chicago had a steel frame. Many people call it the first skyscraper in the world. Steel enabled buildings to grow higher and higher.

The guide also explained that the river is connected to other waters. "The river is connected to Lake Michigan," she said. "And through a canal and other rivers, it is connected to the Mississippi River." She also said that the 5 Great Lakes combined hold about 20 percent of the fresh water on the surface of the Earth.

In the afternoon, Tom and Jack went to the United Center, where the Chicago Bulls play basketball. Tom had loved the Bulls as a boy. "Between 1991 and 1998, the Bulls won 6 championships," he told Jack. "The 1996 squad won 72 games in one season. People still say it was one of the best squads ever."

Then Tom bought Jack a red Bulls jersey with the number 23, the number of Michael Jordan. "If I wore this jersey at every game, I would play much better," Jack said. Tom smiled. "Maybe one day your team will win a championship too."

Questions:
Where is Chicago?
Chicago is in Illinois, next to Lake Michigan.
Why could the fire destroy so many buildings so quickly?
It could destroy them quickly because most buildings were made of wood.
Who did many people blame for the fire?
They blamed Catherine O'Leary, because people said a cow had kicked over a lamp in her barn.
What did the city say in 1997?
In 1997, the city said officially that the fire was not her fault.
How much fresh water do the 5 Great Lakes combined hold?
Combined, they hold about 20 percent of the fresh water on the surface of the Earth.
How many championships did the Bulls win between 1991 and 1998?
They won 6 championships.

lessons.title: An Email from Washington, D.C.
lessons.summary: On a school trip, Emma writes to her grandmother about the Capitol, a senator and the Supreme Court.
lessons.text:
Hi Grandma,

I'm writing to you from our hotel in Washington, D.C. Our class has been here for 3 days, and I have so much to tell you!

Today we visited the Capitol, the big white building where Congress works. Our guide informed us that Congress has 2 parts: the Senate and the House of Representatives. There are 100 senators, 2 from each state, and 435 members of the House. The leader of the House is called the Speaker.

We were lucky, because we met one of the senators from our state for a few minutes. She was very kind and answered our questions. One boy asked her if politicians ever agree with each other. She laughed and said, "More often than you think! Most politicians really want to help people." She also told us that the Capitol is often called "the people's house," because it belongs to all Americans. I liked that idea of the people's house a lot. If I were a senator, I would bring a different class to the Capitol every week!

Then our guide showed us the west side of the Capitol. Since 1981, most new presidents have sworn to protect the Constitution there. Our guide informed us that a new president swears this in front of thousands of people on January 20.

After lunch, we walked across the street to the Supreme Court. The Supreme Court is the highest court in the country, and it has 9 judges, who are called justices. We weren't allowed to take pictures in the room where the justices work, and we weren't allowed to talk there either. Then a speaker gave us a short talk about the history of the court. The speaker was a law student, and she was really interesting.

Tomorrow we have to write a short report. Our teacher gave each student a different topic. My topic is the Supreme Court, and my friend Lily's topic is the Senate. I think I have the best topic!

Regarding your question about the weather, it has been warm and nice. And regarding the food, it's good, but not as good as yours!

I'll see you on Sunday.

Love,
Emma

Questions:
What are the 2 parts of Congress?
The 2 parts of Congress are the Senate and the House of Representatives.
How many senators are there?
There are 100 senators, 2 from each state.
Why is the Capitol called "the people's house"?
It is called "the people's house" because it belongs to all Americans.
What does a new president swear on January 20?
A new president swears to protect the Constitution.
What weren't the students allowed to do?
They weren't allowed to take pictures or to talk in the room where the justices work.

lessons.title: A Day in the Museums
lessons.summary: Omar spends a day in the free museums of Washington, D.C., and ends it at the Lincoln Memorial.
lessons.text:
Omar had always loved museums. When he visited Washington, D.C., he decided to spend a whole day in them. The Smithsonian has 21 museums, most of them in Washington, and all of them are free.

He started at the National Air and Space Museum. When Omar was a boy, he had dreamed of becoming a pilot, so he was very excited. He saw the plane of Orville and Wilbur Wright. In 1903, in North Carolina, it became the first plane with an engine to fly with a pilot. Orville was the pilot, and the first flight lasted only 12 seconds. Omar also saw things from the trips to the moon. "Honestly, I could stay here all week," he thought.

Next, he went to the Museum of Natural History. It has more than 140 million objects, for instance animals, rocks, plants and bones. A guide told him that many scientists work there. "Our scientists investigate how life on Earth has changed," she said. "For instance, they investigate very old bones to learn about animals that lived long ago." Omar read about the scientific work in the museum. He did not understand every scientific word, but he enjoyed learning.

After lunch, Omar visited the Library of Congress, the largest library in the world. It has millions of books, and a lot of them are literature from many countries and many centuries. Omar loves literature, so he could have stayed there for hours.

In the evening, he walked to the Lincoln Memorial. He read that Abraham Lincoln had worked as a postmaster in a small town in Illinois when he was young. "A postmaster who became president!" Omar thought. Then he stood on the steps where Martin Luther King gave a famous speech in 1963. In that speech, King talked about his vision of a country where all people are equal. It was an emotional moment for Omar, and he saw that other people were emotional too.

On the way back to his hotel, Omar was tired, but happy. "Honestly, this was one of the best days of my life," he said to himself.

Questions:
Why was Omar excited at the National Air and Space Museum?
He was excited because he had dreamed of becoming a pilot when he was a boy.
Who was the pilot of the first flight in 1903?
Orville Wright was the pilot.
What do the scientists at the Museum of Natural History investigate?
They investigate how life on Earth has changed.
What did Lincoln do when he was young?
He worked as a postmaster in a small town in Illinois.
What vision did King talk about in his speech?
He talked about his vision of a country where all people are equal.

lessons.title: Yellowstone in Winter
lessons.summary: Nora and her brother visit Yellowstone in the snow, see Old Faithful and watch a fox hunt.
lessons.text:
Nora and her brother Sam had visited Yellowstone National Park in summer. This year, they wanted to see it in winter, when it is covered with snow. Most of the roads are closed to cars then, so they traveled into the park in a special bus that can drive on snow.

Their guide, Linda, had studied environmental science. "Yellowstone became the first national park in the world in 1872," she said. "At that time, this land wasn't part of a state yet. It was a territory. Today most of the park is in Wyoming, and small parts are in Montana and Idaho. The park is named after the Yellowstone River. Many people think the river got its name from yellow rocks. In the park, the river runs through a deep canyon with yellow rocks on its walls."

Later, they stopped at Old Faithful and waited a few minutes. Suddenly, hot water and steam shot high into the air, and everyone took pictures. Around the hot water, people have to walk on special paths. "It's illegal to leave the paths here," Linda said. "The ground can break, and the water under it is very hot."

Then they drove past a forest of small trees. "In 1988, big fires burned about a third of the park," Linda said. "But the fires helped the forest too. The heat opened the pine cones, and millions of seeds fell on the ground. New trees grew from those seeds." Nora had never thought that fire could help a forest. Environmental scientists still study the new forest.

In the afternoon, they saw 2 wolves far away. "Wolves often chase elk," Linda said. "Sometimes they chase them for a long way."

Then Nora saw a red fox in the snow. The fox was standing very still and listening. Suddenly, it jumped high into the air and went head first into the snow. "That's the fox's trick," Linda said. "It can hear a mouse under the snow." "I like that trick!" Sam said.

Questions:
How did Nora and Sam travel into the park?
They traveled in a special bus that can drive on snow.
What was the land in 1872?
In 1872, the land was a territory, not a state.
What is the park named after?
It is named after the Yellowstone River, and many people think the river got its name from yellow rocks.
What is illegal near Old Faithful?
It's illegal to leave the special paths.
How did the fires help the forest?
The heat opened the pine cones, and new trees grew from their seeds.
What is the fox's trick?
It listens for a mouse under the snow, then jumps high and goes head first into the snow.

lessons.title: Two Days on the Train
lessons.summary: A young man takes the train from Chicago to Seattle and makes a friend on the way.
lessons.text:
Last summer, I took the train from Chicago to Seattle. Most people fly, because the plane takes only about 4 hours. The train takes about 46 hours! But I had always wanted to make this long journey across the north of the country by train.

The train is called the Empire Builder. A bed in a small sleeping room was very expensive, so I bought a seat. A seat was much less expensive, and it was big and nice.

The train left Chicago in the afternoon. In the evening, we crossed the Mississippi River. Before I went to sleep, I read about the history of the train. It was named after James Hill, a man who had built a railroad across the north more than 100 years ago. In the era of steam trains, the engines burned coal, and men worked hard all day to put coal into the fire. In that era, the journey took much longer than now.

The next morning, a woman came to the seat next to mine. "Excuse me, is this seat free?" she asked. "Of course," I said. Her name was Grace, and she was going to visit her daughter in Seattle. We started to chat, and we chatted for hours. Grace was a drama teacher at a high school. She told me about the plays that her drama students were doing this year. I told her about the plot of my book, and she told me about the plot of her favorite play.

Later, Grace said, "Excuse me again. Can you do me a favor? Could you watch my bag while I go to get some coffee?" I said yes. When she came back, she had 2 cups. "One is for you," she said. "Thank you for the favor."

On the second evening, we saw the mountains of Glacier National Park in Montana. Everyone came to the windows to look. "I have been taking this train for twenty years," Grace said, "and I never get tired of this view." Twenty years!

On the morning of the third day, we arrived in Seattle. My journey was over, but I had made a new friend.

Questions:
How long does the journey from Chicago to Seattle take by train?
It takes about 46 hours.
Why did the writer buy a seat?
He bought a seat because a bed in a sleeping room was very expensive.
What did the engines burn in the era of steam trains?
They burned coal.
What favor did Grace ask for?
She asked the writer to watch her bag while she went to get some coffee.
How long has Grace been taking this train?
She has been taking this train for twenty years.

lessons.title: A New Job in Seattle
lessons.summary: Priya moves to Seattle for a tech job, and her friend shows her the city, its history and its crows.
lessons.text:
Priya had just finished college when she got a job at a tech company in Seattle. Seattle is in Washington State, in the far northwest of the country.

One weekend, her friend Ana showed her the city. "Seattle has a lot of tech companies," Ana said. "Microsoft and Amazon both have their main offices near here, and many companies invest a lot of money in this city. People invest here because they think the city will keep growing. Amazon started in 1994 by selling books on the internet. Today it has huge distribution centers all over the world. From a distribution center, packages go to people's homes."

"And Boeing builds planes north of the city," Ana said. "A plane has millions of components, and many of those components come from other countries." Priya had not known that a plane needed so many components.

Next, Ana told her about the history of Seattle. "In 1896, people found gold in the north of Canada," she said. "When the news came to Seattle in 1897, the Klondike Gold Rush started. During the rush, thousands of people came to Seattle on their way north. They bought food and tools here, so the city grew very fast."

Then they went to Pike Place Market, which opened in 1907. They walked past fish, flowers and a lot of fresh fruit. "Washington is the biggest producer of apples in the United States," Ana said. "It is also a big producer of other fruit."

"So what is the identity of Seattle?" Priya asked. "I think coffee, rain and tech are all part of the city's identity," Ana said and laughed.

On the way home, they saw some black crows in a tree. "Seattle has a lot of crows," Ana said. "Scientists here have studied the intelligence of crows. They found that crows can remember a person's face for years! Crows also find a mate and usually stay with the same mate for life."

Questions:
Where is Seattle?
Seattle is in Washington State, in the far northwest of the country.
What goes from a distribution center to people's homes?
Packages go from a distribution center to people's homes.
Why did thousands of people come to Seattle during the gold rush?
They came on their way north, and they bought food and tools in Seattle.
What is Washington the biggest producer of?
Washington is the biggest producer of apples in the United States.
What is part of the city's identity?
Coffee, rain and tech are part of the city's identity.
What have scientists found about the intelligence of crows?
They found that crows can remember a person's face for years.

lessons.title: A Quiet Week in Maine
lessons.summary: Emily spends a week on the coast of Maine, sees a lighthouse and an old jail, rows a small boat and watches puffins.
lessons.text:
Emily worked in a busy office in Atlanta, and she needed a rest. She wanted to go somewhere quiet, so she chose the coast of Maine, in the far northeast of the country. She took a domestic flight to Portland, Maine. It was a short domestic flight, and it was not expensive. Before she left, the hotel had confirmed her room by email, and a boat company had confirmed her ticket for a bird tour.

It was summer, but the hotel had told her to bring appropriate clothes. "The wind from the sea can be cold," the email said. "A warm jacket is appropriate even in July."

On her first day, Emily visited Portland Head Light, a white lighthouse on the rocks. It was first lit in 1791. A sign told her that many lighthouses once had a fog bell. The bell was intended to help ships when the fog was too heavy to see the light. It was intended to tell them, "Stay away from the rocks!"

The next day, she drove south to the town of York. There she saw an old jail from 1719. Today the jail is a museum, and people can walk inside its small, dark rooms.

Then she drove to a small fishing town. The harbor was very quiet. A few men were sitting near their boats and repairing their traps for lobsters. One of them, an old man named Walt, told her, "We repair the traps every summer. The sea breaks a lot of them." He also had a small boat, and he let Emily row it in the harbor. She had never rowed a boat before. At first it was hard, but after a few minutes she could row in a straight line.

On her last day, Emily went on the bird tour. The boat took her to a small island. There were many puffins on the rocks, with black and white bodies and bright colors on their faces. "They're so cute!" Emily said. All the people on the boat agreed that the birds were very cute.

Questions:
Why did Emily choose the coast of Maine?
She chose it because she wanted to go somewhere quiet.
Why did the hotel tell her to bring appropriate clothes?
It told her because the wind from the sea can be cold.
What was the fog bell intended to do?
It was intended to help ships when the fog was too heavy to see the light.
What did Emily see in York?
She saw an old jail from 1719, which is now a museum.
Why do the men repair their traps every summer?
They repair them because the sea breaks a lot of them.

lessons.title: The Geography Examination
lessons.summary: Lily prepares for a geography examination about the Mississippi River and learns a trick to spell its name.
lessons.text:
Lily was 13, and she lived in Ohio. In 2 weeks, her class was going to have a geography examination. The topic of the examination was the Mississippi River. Lily was worried. "I'm bad at geography," she told her mother. "I'm going to fail the examination."

"You need a better attitude," her mother said. "With a good attitude, you can learn anything. Let's study together." Lily agreed to try.

First, they looked at a map. Her mother explained that the Mississippi starts as a small stream at a lake in Minnesota. Then it flows south for about 2,300 miles. It passes 10 states, and it ends in the sea south of New Orleans.

Next, Lily wrote down some definitions. A definition explains what a word means. Her teacher had given the class a list of words, for instance "source" and "delta." Lily wrote, "Definition of a source: the place where a river starts." Then she wrote, "Definition of a delta: the land at the end of a river, where it meets the sea."

But Lily had one more problem. She could not spell the word "Mississippi." She always forgot how many letters to write. Her mother smiled. "I have a trick," she said. "When I was a girl, I learned to spell it like this: M, I, double S, I, double S, I, double P, I." Lily said it 5 times, and then she could spell it without looking.

Every evening, Lily studied for an hour. Her mother gave her small map problems to solve, and Lily liked to solve them. After a week, there was a big improvement. Her teacher noticed the improvement too. "There is a good possibility that you will do very well," she said. Lily thought about that possibility with a smile.

The examination had a written part and a spoken part. In the spoken part, Lily answered questions in front of a panel of 3 teachers. The panel asked her to spell "Mississippi," and she did it without a mistake. A week later, she got her results. She had passed the examination with a very high grade. "Your attitude made the difference," her mother said.

Questions:
What was the topic of the geography examination?
The topic was the Mississippi River.
What did Lily's mother say about her attitude?
She said that Lily needed a better attitude.
What is the definition of a source?
A source is the place where a river starts.
How did Lily learn to spell "Mississippi"?
She learned a trick from her mother.
What did the panel of 3 teachers ask her to do?
The panel asked her to spell "Mississippi."
